Subject: Tiered Dedicated Onramp — initial ask

Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move forward but need a pragmatic ramp that aligns with our product milestone cadence and FY27 budget cycles. High level ask: a 3-year commitment with an annual prepay that scales GPU/TPM capacity over the first 12 months in defined mileposts. Key constraints from our side:

- Year 1 cash: 40% of year 1 list spend available at PO.
- Need the ability to double capacity ahead of schedule if usage beats estimates (with a short notice top-up invoice).
- Prefer discounts to be frontloaded on year 1 prepay and then a fixed annual rate years 2–3.
- Tax and invoicing must be to AltumAI in CA; payments run on NET45.

Can you propose a milepost schedule (month-by-month GPU/TPM targets), associated discount tiers by achieved commit, and the invoice cadence? Also please note any SLAs or SLO credits tied to Dedicated availability.

Olivia
Olivia Zhang
Head of Platform Ops, AltumAI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Tiered Dedicated Onramp — initial ask

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear constraints. I've sketched a pragmatic milepost approach that preserves predictability for both sides while offering flexibility on the execution path. Summary below; I'll attach a term sheet draft if this direction looks good.

Proposal (high level):
- Commitment: 3-year reserved capacity with annual prepay option.
- Year 1 onramp (12 months): 4 mileposts at months 0, 3, 6, 12. Each milepost converts an additional tranche of GPU and TPM into the reserved pool.
  - Month 0 (launch): 25% of Year1 target capacity online.
  - Month 3: +25% (50% cumulative).
  - Month 6: +25% (75% cumulative).
  - Month 12: remaining 25% (100% Year1 target).
- Discounting: tied to committed annual prepay amount (frontloaded). Example: 12% off list if Year1 prepay >= 80% of Year1 list; 8% off if prepay between 50–79%; 4% off if prepay 25–49%.
- Acceleration: ability to top-up capacity mid-year at a reduced onramp fee (we propose a 50% step-up fee on the marginal tranche) — invoiceable immediately.
- Invoicing: Year1 prepay billed at PO acceptance (NET45); subsequent year prepay billed at anniversary. For top-ups, invoice NET30.
- SLA credits: Standard Dedicated SLA applies; availability credits defined per term sheet (we'll provide concrete SLA table).

If that direction looks reasonable I can circulate a v3 term sheet with milepost table and a worked example of cost by month.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding finance context from Redwood's side so AltumAI gets a full picture. A couple of clarifications:

- Discount cadence: we prefer to give higher effective discount via Year1 prepay (as Ben sketched) but keep years 2–3 at a flat contracted unit price. That makes forecasting easier for Redwood and satisfies your desire for frontloaded savings.
- Amortization: Redwood can offer an option to amortize Year1 prepay across the 12-month mileposts for accounting purposes (we'll include an amortization schedule in the term sheet).
- Early termination: standard contract language applies; if AltumAI reduces committed capacity materially outside agreed mileposts we have breakage terms. We can propose a carve-out for force-majeure and unpredictable spikes tied to clear usage thresholds.
- Net45 is fine; our default payment terms require an invoice holdback for onboarding credits (we'll call out in term sheet).

I'll coordinate with legal on clean termination language and share the amended term sheet.
